subject: Stewardship note: OKR touchpoint — capacity, GPU unit-econ & cache risks
messages:
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, alice.hughes@horizonai.com
Cc: infrapartner@cloudcorp.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stewardship note: OKR touchpoint — capacity, GPU unit-econ & cache risks

Team — quick note ahead of the QBR prep cycle. I ran a fresh pass on the capacity model and wanted to highlight a few items for leadership to weigh in on before we lock the QBR deck. Attached: capacity_model_v2.xlsx and a one-pager with the topline.

Topline asks:
- Confirm whether we treat August usage spike as an aberration or the new baseline for runway calc (affects committed vs burst mix).
- Agree on the aggressiveness of batching/cache trade-offs for latency-sensitive hosted customers (we can save ~18–24% token cost but see P50 latency impact for <256 token flows).
- Decision on whether we surface an interim quantization recommendation for Dedicated customers this quarter (saves infra $/token but requires compatibility testing).

Quick notes from the model: 
- GPU spend delta across scenarios (conservative / optimistic) ranges from +14% to -9% for H2 unless we increase caching hit-rate by ~10 p.p.
- Utilization tail risk: single-region saturation events (e.g., APAC burst) push utilization past 95% for the N1 pool; fallback to N2 variants still increases cost per token by ~35%.

Plan: sync with leadership tomorrow 10:30 PT for a 30m touchpoint. If we can close the three asks above, I’ll finalize the QBR infra slide and cost appendix.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Director, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: qbr_one_pager.pdf (two-page PDF)

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stewardship note: OKR touchpoint — capacity, GPU unit-econ & cache risks

Thanks Dylan — good concise framing. A few quick responses inline: 

- August spike: Looks correlated with two PLG campaigns (trial churn and high-embedding churn). My recommendation: treat as elevated but not baseline for reserved capacity. Use burstables + stricter quota for anonymous usage to reduce commit needs.

- Batching/cache: Agree we can push conservative caching in Hosted (increase prefix-cache windows for steady-state flows). For latency-sensitive routes (chat-short), let's keep current cache TTLs and instead prioritize micro-batching improvements (smoother scheduling) — that yields ~9–12% cost benefit without P50 latency regressions.

- Quantization for Dedicated: I support an opt-in quantized image for early adopters with a CHURN testing plan (two-week canary) rather than org-wide default this quarter. We should include compatibility caveats in the QBR appendix.

I’ll bring these notes to the 10:30 touchpoint and escalate any remaining open asks. I attached a short comment sheet (inline tab in the spreadsheet).

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: alice.hughes@horizonai.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stewardship note: OKR touchpoint — capacity, GPU unit-econ & cache risks

On Mon, Aug 30, 2027 at 09:12 AM dylan.brooks@redwood.com wrote:
> Team — quick note ahead of the QBR prep cycle. I ran a fresh pass on the capacity model and wanted to highlight a few items for leadership to weigh in on before we lock the QBR deck.

Two operational flags from infra: 
1) Queueing risk: if we push micro-batching without increasing per-GPU concurrency ceilings, we could amplify tail latency during burst windows. Need to validate scheduler changes against the N1/N2 pool mix.
2) Billing reconciliation: if we increase cache hit-rate assumptions in runbooks, finance will require an audit trail (data pipeline and sample queries) to justify lower forecasted token spend. That will add ~3 business days to the QBR prep timeline if we produce the audit artifacts.

From my side, I ran a short stress test against the N1 pool and attached the results to the spreadsheet (stress_results_tab). The concern: the nominal 95% utilization number masks 10s spikes that push queue depth up and degrade TTL-based caching benefit. Without config changes to eviction policy, estimated cost savings from cache look ~6–8% rather than 18–24%.

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
Attachment referenced: stress_results_tab (spreadsheet tab)

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, alice.hughes@horizonai.com, infrapartner@cloudcorp.com
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stewardship note: OKR touchpoint — capacity, GPU unit-econ & cache risks

Thanks — good points all. Quick summary / decisions from the touchpoint and follow-ups: 

Decisions made:
- Treat August as an elevated baseline for PLG-informed demand but do NOT increase reserved commitments this quarter. We’ll rely on burst capacity + quota adjustments.
- Push micro-batching improvements but gate rollout behind scheduler-concurrency validation (Markus to own).
- Offer quantized Dedicated option as opt-in; Product will own the canary and comms.

Action items (owners / due):
- Markus: complete scheduler validation and send a brief by Sep 6 ("scheduler-validation-v1.pdf").
- Lauren: update QBR slides with recommended canary language + callout on finance audit expectations by Sep 2.
- Vivek: run a short billing sample (7k queries) to show cache-hit attribution and hand to Finance for reconciliation by Sep 3.
- Dylan: finalize QBR infra appendix and upload to Drive (target Sep 4).

I'll assemble the updated appendix and share the final slide pack once the artifacts land. If anyone has a last-minute objection to the canary approach, flag it in-thread by EOD Sep 1.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Director, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: scheduler-validation-v1.pdf (pending), capacity_model_v2.xlsx (updated)
